title: Book One · Chapter 61: The Closed Rice Shop
story:
Later on Monday, Mum finishes her sewing early. Her customer comes to collect the work. The blue-bowl shop is now open again. There is time to ask before supper. Ronan takes his map. Mum comes with him. Leo comes with them too.

The old rice shop has no rice in it.

Ronan puts his face near the window. There is a broken chair behind the glass. A long line of dust lies below it.

“Perhaps the gate is inside,” Leo says.

“Then we cannot use it.”

Mum stands beside them. She comes to ask about Mrs Gao. Mrs Lan still has the brown envelope at home. No one opened it.

Mr Qiu told them about an old path behind this shop. Someone at the blue-bowl shop may know another entrance. Ronan drew that path on a loose piece of paper. It ends in a question mark.

Leo points down the side of the building.

“There.”

A narrow path runs beside a wall. A board stands across it.

Mum reads the board. “Closed. We need another way.”

“I can get under that,” Leo says.

“You can fit under it,” Mum says. “But the path is closed. We cannot use it.”

She turns towards the next shop. Blue bowls stand in its window. Mr Qiu told them to look for those. A woman is washing a large bowl outside. Mum asks her about East Court.

The woman points back along the street.

“Past the tea shop. There is a gate beside a wall with white stones on top. The gate looks like part of the wall.”

“Is it green?” Ronan asks.

“It is. Many gates are green.”

Ronan looks down at his map. He drew a very large green gate. But he left the tea shop off the map.

They walk back. Leo counts the doors. Ronan looks for the white stones. Mum carries their cloth bag. Their empty lunch bowls are inside it. They have other work to do today too.

The tea shop is easy to see. Steam rises from a pot by its door. Beside it is a high wall. Three white stones sit on top.

“There are only three,” Leo says.

“That is enough stones,” Mum tells him.

The gate is shut. There is no number on it.

Ronan wants to knock. Then he looks at Mum.

“Shall we ask here?”

Mum nods. She knocks twice.

A man opens the gate a little. He is holding one wet shoe. Water runs from its heel onto the ground.

“Is this the way to East Court?” Mum asks.

“Yes. Who do you want?”

“Mrs Gao. Number six.”

“The little house at the back. But she is at work now.”

Mum explains about the envelope. The man listens. He does not reach for her bag.

“Come after supper,” he says. “She will be home.”

Ronan draws three small circles above a new gate. He writes TEA beside the right building.

“Can people come through this gate every day?” he asks.

“Until dark. Then we lock it.”

The old map does not show the gate times yet.

On the walk home, Leo reaches for the pencil.

“I can draw the wet shoe.”

“It is a street map,” Ronan says.

“The shoe was in the street.”

Mum stops and moves the bag to her other hand. She smiles at both boys.

“Leave space for the gate first.”

At the corner, they meet a woman with two heavy bags. Mum asks, “Do you know that gate?” The woman nods. She uses a different entrance after dark. Ronan does not add that way yet. He puts a small line beside his question mark. There are things to ask next time.

Ronan makes space. In the corner, away from the road, Leo draws a very wet shoe.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- closed＝关闭的
- beside＝在旁边
- after supper＝晚饭后
- leave space＝留空位

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：entrance＝入口；steam＝蒸汽；heel＝鞋跟。

## 读句提示

**Ronan takes his map.**

Ronan／拿起／他的地图。先找人，再找动作。

## 理解问题

1. 他们为什么不能穿过米店旁的小路？
2. Ronan给地图补上了哪些有用的信息？
